entry.title: Music Transformer, reproduced and running in the browser
entry.summary: The released Music Transformer configuration, re-implemented in PyTorch and trained for one million steps on the official MAESTRO v1 split, reaches validation NLL 1.835 on the selection metric (the paper reports 1.835), 1.827 on every validation event and 1.801 on test; the port matches the original Tensor2Tensor code to float32 rounding, and the trained model now runs in the browser at 29 ms per event with a pianist-or-model blind test.

entry.title: What the reader keeps and what the singer keeps
entry.summary: On clean engravings open OMR reads both hands and the chord tones completely (homr 100% of K. 545, also from a phone photograph), so the 79–86% on commercial sheets is a layout and typography gap; YuE2 sings She in register but keeps 37% of the line against a 71% ceiling; MusicGen-melody, with no notation input, follows the same lines better (96% of She in order, an 18-note run), and EnCodec loses none of the harmony.

entry.title: Where the score gets lost
entry.summary: YuE2's score input is a lead sheet: a third of the printed notes can be sent at all, OMR reads the melody but no chord symbols, the melody that is sent comes back loosely (80% recall alone, worse with chord symbols), and Stable Audio Open keeps the recording's harmony but not its register.

entry.title: YuE2 experiments in musical control
entry.summary: YuE2 produced an acceptable original song from lyrics and style, but score-conditioned arrangements and vocal layering were less convincing in my listening.

entry.title: Audio to score and a test of symbolic control
entry.summary: Promote direct audio-to-score research into the core reading path, correct its treatment in the report, and evaluate explicit melody control with YuE2 after unsuccessful ACE-Step listening tests.

entry.title: Music to score, score to music: the anatomy of a song generator
entry.summary: Three Suno uploads of one piano recording came back as audio and nothing readable. A technical report dissects why — codec-token language models through four lenses — and specifies the inverse: a notation-native latent that transcribes in and renders out, with latent actions as the edit primitive.

entry.title: From data to a labelled dataset: the David Foster corpus
entry.summary: The ACE experiment gets its corpus: 28 David Foster songs from two albums and a YouTube compilation, cut as whole songs, with captions drafted from the audio and confirmed by ear in a private web workbench.

entry.title: ACE moves from idea to runnable experiment
entry.summary: An ACE-Step 1.5 fine-tuning pipeline now passes a synthetic end-to-end CPU smoke. Real ACE weights, the RTX PRO 5000 run, and original piano data are next.

entry.title: From a research agenda to a product musicians can use
entry.summary: Music Kitchen takes shape as a personal arranging studio. The key question becomes how a musician directs the second and third revision through sound, examples, and gestures.
